Grain
grān
n. (a single seed; rendering Greek kokkos)
From Latin granum, a seed. Scripture's interest is almost always in the single grain — the smallest possible unit, and what it does.

Biblical Definition

A grain is one seed. Christ makes it the measure of sufficient faith: “If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove” (Mat 17:20). He makes it the law of His own death: “Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit” (Joh 12:24). Paul answers the resurrection question with it — “thou sowest not that body that shall be… but bare grain” (1Co 15:37).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines grain as any small hard mass; a single seed or hard seed of a plant, particularly of those kinds whose seeds are used for food of man or beast.

expand to see more

GRAIN, n. Any small hard mass; as a grain of sand.

2. A single seed or hard seed of a plant, particularly of those kinds whose seeds are used for food of man or beast.

3. Grain, without a definitive, signifies corn in general.

Key Scripture

Mat 17:20 — "And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you."

Joh 12:24 — "Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit."

1Co 15:37 — "And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other grain:"

Luk 17:6 — "And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you."

Modern Corruption

Faith is measured by quantity and intensity, and Christ measured it by a seed — the smallest thing in the field, and alive.

expand to see more

The mustard seed answer was given to disciples who had just failed to cast out a demon and asked why. Christ's reply names not the size of their faith but its absence: because of your unbelief… if ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed. The comparison is not quantitative encouragement so much as a redefinition — what matters is that faith is living and rightly directed, not that it is large. A mountain does not move because of the volume of belief applied to it.

John 12:24 states the law by which everything fruitful in the kingdom operates, and Christ applies it first to Himself and then to His followers: he that loveth his life shall lose it. A grain kept safe abides alone. That is the whole cost and the whole promise of discipleship in one agricultural sentence.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek kokkos (G2848), a grain or kernel; sitos (G4621), wheat — the corn of wheat in John 12:24.

expand to see more

Greek kokkos (G2848) — grain, kernel; Matthew 17:20, John 12:24, 1 Corinthians 15:37.

Greek sinapi (G4615) — mustard; Matthew 13:31, the least of all seeds.

Usage

"“Faith as a grain of mustard seed” — living and directed, not large."

"“Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die” — the law of all fruitfulness."

"“Thou sowest… bare grain” — Paul on the resurrection body."
